title: “Kya family planning after marriage hoti hai?”: Integrating Cultural Sensitivity in an LLM Chatbot for Reproductive Health

bias_targets.methodology: Qualitative analysis of user prompts and chatbot responses to evaluate the system's handling of cultural taboos, community practices, and local norms regarding sexual and reproductive health.
Evaluating the chatbot's comprehension of code-mixed language (Hinglish), regional dialects, grammatical errors, and its reliance on complex medical terminology versus accessible, localized language.
Analyzing chatbot responses to queries about family planning responsibilities and reproductive health to see if the model reinforces or challenges traditional gender roles and patriarchal norms.
Assessing whether the chatbot's healthcare recommendations (such as suggesting IVF) account for the financial constraints and limited healthcare access of users from underserved communities.
Examining how the chatbot navigates conflicts between evidence-based medical advice and specific religious beliefs or prohibitions regarding procedures like sterilization and family planning.
